Division: Youth
No entry fee. The sanctioned Youth Division is open to JRTCA child and/or youth members in the following age brackets: Child Handler (ages 5 thru 9) and Youth Handler (ages 10 thru 16). A child/youth exhibitor’s age is determined as of January 1st of the current calendar year except for those children turning five years of age. They may begin competing in Child Handler any time following their firth birthday. All exhibitors in the Youth Division must be current JRTCA members, either under a Family membership or under an individual Youth membership. Youths or their families applying for a JRTCA membership at a Sanctioned Trial will be allowed to enter classes at that trial. Youth exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Youth Handling and Youth Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Youth High Score & Reserve. Child exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Child Handling and Child Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Child High Score & Reserve (non-sanctioned). A tie will be broken with the final decision made by a conformation judge other than the judge of the day. The tiebreaker takes place in the conformation ring and is determined at the judge's discretion by the exhibitor's handling/presentation of his/her terrier, by the answers to the judge's questions, or by a combination of the two. Note: If there is no other available conformation judge on the grounds, then the judge of the day will determine the tiebreaker. For a full set of rules, go to https:// www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/youth.php. Also see the JRTCA Child and Youth Handbook and Study Guide at www.therealjackrussell.com/download/2017_JRTCA_YouthStudyGuide.pdf.

Division: Racing
Sponsor: FireN TheHole Jack Russell Terriers
JUDGE'S BRIEFING AT 8:15 A.M. Adult terriers may not cross-enter between regular racing classes, veteran racing classes and senior racing classes. Racing champions are determined by a run-off of the first-place terrier in each class in each section. Racing ribbons presented in main pavilion after racing is completed. Qualifications for Championship Run Off: A. Terriers must place 1st in a Flat or Hurdle race final to qualify for Championship Run Offs. B. A terrier MUST ENTER AND FINISH in both, at least one flat AND one hurdle race at the beginning level based on trial entries (heat, semi, final). C. A terrier must continue to advance, if qualified, to all additional semi-final heats up to the final champion race. If injured, the terrier is then finished and cannot race in final. D. A FINISHED race is when the terrier runs down the track unassisted (by owner or anyone else) with a secured muzzle to the backside of the barrier. E. In the event a terrier does not meet all the above criteria, the second-place terrier in the final of that class (either flats or hurdles) will qualify for the championship run off if they meet the criteria as outlined above. (01/20) The rulebook is available at www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/rulebook.php. For other information about racing, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/racing.php.

Division: Go-to-Ground
A timed event that simulates the terrier's natural instinct to hunt. The terrier enters an artificial den/tunnel to demonstrate its working ability. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from G-T-G at this trial.) Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. The judge may halt the work if the judge believes the terrier is injuring itself.

Division: Super Earth
A more challenging G-T-G course with a series of false entrances and/or false tunnels and dens. Open to any terrier, 6 months and older. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from Super Earth at this trial.)Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. Timing for all Super Earth classes: One second per foot of tunnel to reach quarry; may leave and re- enter the earth multiple times until quarry is reached; work quarry for one minute without a break in work and without leaving quarry. Terrier is not to leave quarry once it is reached. Height is limited to 15" and under.

Division: Trailing & Locating
Trailing & Locating is a sanctioned event that involves the terrier tracking and locating a quarry above ground. The terrier is judged on his ability to follow a line in a simulated natural hunting environment, to locate, mark and open on the quarry. The terrier is judged on a combination of time and accuracy. The terrier with the fastest time is not necessarily the winner. Course length is a minimum of 50 steps long with at least two direction changes but no more than four direction changes. Event is in a fenced area. The trail is scented with mixture of rat excrement, water, and unscented glycerin.

Division: Agility
All terriers must be at least one year of age to compete in JRTCA Agility or practice on any equipment. Agility (Absolutely no Flexi-Leads – No racing leads, martingale collars or harnesses) Agility will start at 9:15 am with Advanced Agility. $5.00 Practice runs begin at 8:15 am to 9:00 am Run Through payment can be found in the add-on section. Dogs may run naked or wear one flat collar without tags. No other accoutrements are allowed. No food or toys are allowed within 10 feet of the ring. Exceptions are that toys are allowed for the class “A Way to Play”. A Beginner Agility certificate may be earned prior to competing in Advanced Agility & for Agility High Score Champion & Reserve. Move ups from Beginner Agility to Advanced Agility are allowed from trial to trial. (Example: 2nd Beginner leg is earned at Saturday’s trial; the team could move to Advanced Agility for Sunday’s trial). As a JRTCA certificate has not been issued both qualifying score sheets must be presented to move up. Advanced Agility competitors may cross enter the Beginner Agility class For Exhibit Ony (FEO) to be used as a warmup run. No ribbons will be rewarded, and no paperwork completed for an FEO run. Teams with two scores of 190 or greater in the agility classes (Beginner and Advanced) are eligible for agility certificates. Teams with one qualifying score of 200 in Jumpers are eligible for the Jumpers certificate. For a complete set of rules, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/agility.php

Division: Nose Work
Open to dogs six months and older who are capable of alerting to the target odors. Level 1 target odor is birch. Level 2 target odors are birch, anise and clove. A Level 1 title is not required to enter Level 2 classes. Time faults incurred for dropped food, failure to go through start-line marker, excessive disturbance of search area, incorrect call in Level 1 and failure to call finish in Level 2 searches. Eliminating (pee, poop or vomit) in a search area ends the search and results in a non-qualifying score and no placement. Consult the rulebook for more detailed information. First through sixth ribbons for each class determined by correct calls with fastest time first. Champion and reserve champion ribbons awarded to top two JRTs in Level 1 and top two JRTs in Level 2 by combining scores for all elements/classes. Teams with no faults considered first.

Division: Brush Hunt (Non-Sanctioned)
Brush hunt is an above-ground hunting simulation held in a fenced area. One camouflaged tube containing a live rat is hidden within the brush area. The challenge is for the terrier to use natural instincts to successfully locate and work the quarry. Terrier must work to find the quarry in the shortest amount of time. The clock starts when the judge is ready and signals you to release your dog at the gate. All four paws must be on the ground before you release your dog. The judge stops the clock when your dog has found the tube. You do not enter with the dog but you can encourage your dog verbally. No hand signals allowed. The dog must locate the tube to have a qualifying time. No cross-entering between classes. Maximum time allowed is two minutes.

Division: Youth
No entry fee. The sanctioned Youth Division is open to JRTCA child and/or youth members in the following age brackets: Child Handler (ages 5 thru 9) and Youth Handler (ages 10 thru 16). A child/youth exhibitor’s age is determined as of January 1st of the current calendar year except for those children turning five years of age. They may begin competing in Child Handler any time following their firth birthday. All exhibitors in the Youth Division must be current JRTCA members, either under a Family membership or under an individual Youth membership. Youths or their families applying for a JRTCA membership at a Sanctioned Trial will be allowed to enter classes at that trial. Youth exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Youth Handling and Youth Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Youth High Score & Reserve. Child exhibitors must compete in a minimum of Child Handling and Child Go-to-Ground to qualify for the Child High Score & Reserve (non-sanctioned). A tie will be broken with the final decision made by a conformation judge other than the judge of the day. The tiebreaker takes place in the conformation ring and is determined at the judge's discretion by the exhibitor's handling/presentation of his/her terrier, by the answers to the judge's questions, or by a combination of the two. Note: If there is no other available conformation judge on the grounds, then the judge of the day will determine the tiebreaker. For a full set of rules, go to https:// www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/youth.php. Also see the JRTCA Child and Youth Handbook and Study Guide at www.therealjackrussell.com/download/2017_JRTCA_YouthStudyGuide.pdf.

Division: Racing
JUDGE'S BRIEFING AT 8:15 A.M. Adult terriers may not cross-enter between regular racing classes, veteran racing classes and senior racing classes. Racing champions are determined by a run-off of the first-place terrier in each class in each section. Racing ribbons presented in main pavilion after racing is completed. Qualifications for Championship Run Off: A. Terriers must place 1st in a Flat or Hurdle race final to qualify for Championship Run Offs. B. A terrier MUST ENTER AND FINISH in both, at least one flat AND one hurdle race at the beginning level based on trial entries (heat, semi, final). C. A terrier must continue to advance, if qualified, to all additional semi-final heats up to the final champion race. If injured, the terrier is then finished and cannot race in final. D. A FINISHED race is when the terrier runs down the track unassisted (by owner or anyone else) with a secured muzzle to the backside of the barrier. E. In the event a terrier does not meet all the above criteria, the second-place terrier in the final of that class (either flats or hurdles) will qualify for the championship run off if they meet the criteria as outlined above. (01/20) The rulebook is available at www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/rulebook.php. For other information about racing, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/racing.php.

Division: Go-to-Ground
A timed event that simulates the terrier's natural instinct to hunt. The terrier enters an artificial den/tunnel to demonstrate its working ability. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from G-T-G at this trial.) Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. The judge may halt the work if the judge believes the terrier is injuring itself.

Division: Super Earth
A more challenging G-T-G course with a series of false entrances and/or false tunnels and dens. Open to any terrier, 6 months and older. Schooling prior to the competition is not permitted (Any violation of this rule shall result in disqualification from Super Earth at this trial.)Terrier may switch from one type of work to another (examples: baying to concentrated stare or digging to baying.) For Championship Certificate classes, a copy of the certificate must be submitted with pre-entry or be shown to the Den Steward at the time of the class. No cross entering between Certificate classes. Timing for all Super Earth classes: One second per foot of tunnel to reach quarry; may leave and re- enter the earth multiple times until quarry is reached; work quarry for one minute without a break in work and without leaving quarry. Terrier is not to leave quarry once it is reached. Height is limited to 15" and under.

Division: Trailing & Locating
Trailing & Locating is a sanctioned event that involves the terrier tracking and locating a quarry above ground. The terrier is judged on his ability to follow a line in a simulated natural hunting environment, to locate, mark and open on the quarry. The terrier is judged on a combination of time and accuracy. The terrier with the fastest time is not necessarily the winner. Course length is a minimum of 50 steps long with at least two direction changes but no more than four direction changes. Event is in a fenced area. The trail is scented with mixture of rat excrement, water, and unscented glycerin.

Division: Agility
All terriers must be at least one year of age to compete in JRTCA Agility or practice on any equipment. Agility (Absolutely no Flexi-Leads – No racing leads, martingale collars or harnesses) Agility will start at 9:15 am with Advanced Agility. $5.00 Practice runs begin at 8:15 am to 9:00 am Run Through payment can be found in the add-on section. Dogs may run naked or wear one flat collar without tags. No other accoutrements are allowed. No food or toys are allowed within 10 feet of the ring. Exceptions are that toys are allowed for the class “A Way to Play”. A Beginner Agility certificate may be earned prior to competing in Advanced Agility & for Agility High Score Champion & Reserve. Move ups from Beginner Agility to Advanced Agility are allowed from trial to trial. (Example: 2nd Beginner leg is earned at Saturday’s trial; the team could move to Advanced Agility for Sunday’s trial). As a JRTCA certificate has not been issued both qualifying score sheets must be presented to move up. Advanced Agility competitors may cross enter the Beginner Agility class For Exhibit Ony (FEO) to be used as a warmup run. No ribbons will be rewarded, and no paperwork completed for an FEO run. Teams with two scores of 190 or greater in the agility classes (Beginner and Advanced) are eligible for agility certificates. Teams with one qualifying score of 200 in Jumpers are eligible for the Jumpers certificate. For a complete set of rules, go to www.therealjackrussell.com/trial/agility.php

Division: Brush Hunt (Non-Sanctioned)
Brush hunt is an above-ground hunting simulation held in a fenced area. One camouflaged tube containing a live rat is hidden within the brush area. The challenge is for the terrier to use natural instincts to successfully locate and work the quarry. Terrier must work to find the quarry in the shortest amount of time. The clock starts when the judge is ready and signals you to release your dog at the gate. All four paws must be on the ground before you release your dog. The judge stops the clock when your dog has found the tube. You do not enter with the dog but you can encourage your dog verbally. No hand signals allowed. The dog must locate the tube to have a qualifying time. No cross-entering between classes. Maximum time allowed is two minutes.
